note.text: Directed writing provides a situation and specific instructions. Identify your role, audience, purpose and required form before drafting. Underline every content point and decide where it belongs. A fluent response can still fail its purpose if it omits an essential instruction or uses the wrong format. Use a suitable tone and distinguish information given by the task from assumptions. Check the completed text against the directions rather than marking it by length alone.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to adapt content, audience, purpose and form to a stated writing task. Builds on: essay planning and passage evidence. Leads to: formal speeches, talks, articles and letters.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: CLASSROOM MODEL NOTICE. Reading Club Meeting. Members are invited to a planning meeting in the school library on Monday afternoon. We will choose a shared reading activity and agree how to care for borrowed books. Please bring a suggestion and a notebook. Issued by the fictional club secretary. The model gives audience, place, time and purpose without claiming an actual school event.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Make a short checklist from the prompt. Plan the order, draft the required form and check each point. Add only suitable invented details where the task permits them. Do not replace a requested notice with an unrelated essay simply because its sentences are correct.
